newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UN says Angola postpones unity government.
newsitem.headline: UN says Angola postpones unity government.

text.p: U.N. mediators said on Thursday Angola's government and UNITA rivals had postponed the formation of the country's unity government, scheduled for this weekend.

Alioune Blondin Beye, special representative of the United Nations in the southern African country, told a news conference in the capital Luanda that Saturday's inauguration was off after a meeting on Thursday of the U.N.-chaired joint commission, where government and UNITA negotiators were meeting.

"The joint commission has decided to postpone the date of Janurary 25 for the inauguration of a government of national unity and reconciliation. The joint commission has decided to fix for February 12 the day of arrival of UNITA deputies to Luanda," Beye said.

He said a new date for the inauguration, whose postponement had been widely expected, would only be fixed after the deputies from the former rebel movement, which signed a peace accord in 1994 to end two decades of war, had taken up their seats in the united parliament.
